name: Bharat Rural Livelihoods Foundation (BRLF)
supports: 57 CSO partners nationally across the Central Indian Tribal Belt (incl. Odisha); named CSOs include BAIF, AKRSP-I, SRIJAN, Foundation for Ecological Security, PARHIT Consortium, SEWA, PRADAN, and Western Odisha NREGA Consortium (WONC)
notes: Odisha-specific grant total not stated; WONC is the clearest Odisha-specific grantee found

name: Vedanta Aluminium
supports: Own CSR programmes (not CSO grants) in Jharsuguda and Kalahandi districts -- children's education, women's empowerment, healthcare, WASH, agriculture, skilling; claims ~10 lakh people impacted statewide
notes: Direct implementer via own foundation/CSR arm more than a CSO funder

name: National Aluminium Company (NALCO)
supports: Own CSR programmes in Angul and Koraput districts (Damanjodi, Nalconagar) -- community centres, tribal child education (with KISS), infrastructure
notes: PSU; direct implementer via own CSR wing

name: Azim Premji Foundation
supports: Nutrition and early-childhood-care work in unspecified 'remote districts' of Odisha; no dedicated Field Institute in the state (unlike its 61-district presence in 6 other states)
notes: Odisha districts not individually named in sources checked

name: UNICEF
supports: State government, CSOs and CBOs across 15 'nutritionally vulnerable' districts of Odisha (not individually named in source) on WASH and nutrition; partners include Odisha Livelihoods Mission and Water.org on WASH financing
column6: works through district administrations and local CSOs as implementers
